user.title: Cloudflare Abuse Monitor
user.description:
1. Open [Create a Cloudflare API token]({token_url}). The token requires exactly the following permissions:
{permissions}
Verify that all five permissions are listed. If Cloudflare omitted one, add it with **+ Add more**.
2. **Required:** the link preselects all accounts and all zones. Under **Account Resources**, select your account. Under **Zone Resources**, select the zones to be monitored (**Specific zone** for each zone, or **All zones from an account**). The token then has no access to anything else.
3. Create the token and enter it below, together with your AbuseIPDB API key.

In the next step, you select the zones to be monitored; all zones are selected by default. The remaining setup is automatic: one IP list named `block_ips` per Cloudflare account, shared by the zones of that account, and two firewall rules per zone (Block listed IPs, and Skip to log visitors). Each item is created only if it does not already exist. Any missing permission is reported in this dialog.

zones.title: Select zones
zones.description: The token has access to {count} zones that are not yet monitored. Select the zones to be monitored. Each zone is added as a separate device with its own sensors and Under Attack Mode switch. Zones can be added or removed later under **Configure**.

list_select.title: Select the IP list for blocking
list_select.description: Cloudflare did not allow a new IP list to be created for {zone}. The list limit of your plan may have been reached. Select an existing IP list instead. The selected list is used by every zone of that account.

reconfigure.title: Replace the Cloudflare API token
reconfigure.description:
Enter a new API token for {zone_name}. [Create a token]({token_url}) with the following permissions, and add any permission that is missing:
{permissions}
Under **Account Resources**, select your account. Under **Zone Resources**, select the zones that this entry monitors.
An entry that still uses the Global API Key is converted to the token, and the email address and Global API Key are removed.

reauth_confirm.title: A new Cloudflare API token is required

rules_confirm.title: Make room for the firewall rules
rules_confirm.description:
Zone {zone} already has {count} of the {limit} custom rules that its Cloudflare plan allows, and the integration requires {needed} more. To make room, the following changes are proposed:
{changes}

No rule changes what it does, and no rule is removed except the second rule of a merge, whose condition becomes part of the merged rule. Before any change is made, the original rules are saved in Home Assistant. They can be restored at any time with the action `cloudflare_abuse_monitor.restore_rules`, which also removes the rules of the integration.

Nothing is changed until you approve. To cancel, close this dialog.

init.title: Cloudflare Abuse Monitor options
init.description: Select the zones to be monitored. A newly selected zone is set up in the same way as during the initial setup: the permissions are verified, the IP list of its account is used, and the two firewall rules are created if they do not exist. If the zone has no room for the rules, the proposed changes are shown for approval first. When a zone is deselected, its device and entities are removed; its firewall rules and IP list remain in Cloudflare unchanged. The other options apply to every zone of this entry.

data.abuse_confidence_score: AbuseIPDB confidence score classified as high risk (0-100)
data.mode: Mode (Monitor only reports; Active adds high-risk IP addresses to the IP list)
data.recheck_enabled: Check IP addresses again after a number of days
data.recheck_days: Days before an IP address is checked again
data.under_attack_mode: Enable Under Attack Mode automatically on a traffic spike
data.under_attack_request_threshold: Requests per update interval classified as a traffic spike
